title: fix(console): a refused Set as default restores the previous default app
body:
Fixes #34860

Clause-②: no
Metadata-protocol: none

## 维护者速读

- 用户能看到什么变化:管理员在「设置 › 应用」里把一个只读包里的应用设为默认时,服务器拒绝后,原来的默认应用会被放回去,部署不再变成没有默认应用;放回也失败时会多一条错误提示,点名哪个应用已不再是默认。
- 为什么做:替遇到「设为默认」被拒的管理员解决默认应用静默丢失的问题(列表视图同类问题之前已修好,这是应用页的同款)。
- 出错会怎样:只影响这个页面的「设为默认」按钮;写入顺序不变,最坏情况和以前一样是没有默认应用,但现在会明说;可直接撤回本改动。
- 要你做什么:无

## What changes

- **`AppManagementPage` set-default handler.** The order stays demote-first, promote-second. The handler now records each outgoing default whose demotion the server accepted. When a later write fails and that failure is known to have written nothing, it saves each of those apps back with `isDefault: true` through the same `saveApp` helper, so in the same package scope the demotion used, and then shows the original failure. A failure counts as having written nothing when the server answered it with a 4xx refusal (the client puts the status on `httpStatus`; a target in a read-only package answers 403 "Cannot overlay 'app' in package …: that package is read-only"), or when `saveApp` failed before its write was sent (the stored-app read failed or found nothing; `saveApp` marks those throws). In those cases the failed write changed nothing, so the restore cannot make two defaults. Any other failure (no answer, such as a dropped connection or a timeout, or a 5xx) may have been written, so the promote may have landed and a restore could leave two defaults. For those, the handler sends no restore write and keeps the earlier behaviour: the failure toast, then the re-read, which shows the result. A refused demotion leaves nothing to restore and sends no further write.
- **A failed restore is reported.** If the restore fails too, a second error toast names each app that is no longer the default and gives the reasons (identical reasons are listed once). New key `appManagement.toast.restoreDefaultFailed` in all eleven console locales (`@object-ui/i18n`), as a keyed template with a `{{reason}}` hole like the page's other failure toasts.
- **No pre-write refusal.** The page does not know a package is read-only before it writes: the served app row carries `_packageId` only, and the page reads no package writability. The card's other branch (refuse a locked target before any write) would need a new read, and the dispatch ruled out a new server call, so this PR only adds the restore.
- **The list-view precedent.** For list views, Set as Default now writes one patch at a time and stops at the first refusal (`handleSetDefaultView`). Its PR left one case open: the clear lands, the set is refused, and the object has no default view. This PR closes that case for apps, when the refusal is a 4xx.
- **Claim surface.** The surface is amended on the card in comment 7222424773: the eleven locale files, `@object-ui/i18n` in the changeset, and the honestWrites case. The pre-write refusal branch is left out.
- Changeset `.changeset/34860-app-set-default-restore.md`: `@object-ui/console` and `@object-ui/i18n` patch, with both declaration lines.

## Tests

New top-level describe in the existing harness `AppManagementPage.mutations.test.tsx` (the shared-harness rule, ruling record 6583487846). The outgoing default is in a writable package and the target is in a read-only one. The refusals have the shape the client throws (an `Error` with `httpStatus`). Each case asserts every write with the package scope it named, and, where it applies, the default set that the writes which landed leave behind:

- promote refused: the writes are demote → promote (refused) → re-promote of the previous default in its own package. The landed state has the same default as before, one error toast carries the server's refusal, and no success toast is shown;
- restore also refused (403): the same three writes, the landed state has no default, and a second error toast names the app and the restore's reason;
- demotion refused (403): exactly one write, nothing to restore, and the default is unchanged;
- promote failed with no answer (`TypeError('Failed to fetch')`, no `httpStatus`) and promote failed with a 5xx (504): exactly the two writes, no restore write, and one error toast;
- CONTROL, happy path: exactly demote → promote in that order, no restore write, and the default moves.

`AppManagementPage.honestWrites-12300.test.tsx` had a case that pinned the defect ("a demotion that landed is shown": no app is the default after a refused promote). Its refusal now carries `httpStatus: 403`, and it asserts the restore: three writes, and the previous default's row still shows Default.

## Acceptance notes

- **A failure the server did not answer is not undone.** If the promote fails with no answer or with a 5xx, it may have landed. Restoring then could leave two defaults, so the page restores nothing. If that write did not land after all, the deployment is left with no default, as before this PR. The failure toast and the re-read show that state. Only a 4xx refusal, or a failure before the write is sent, is known to have written nothing.
- **Not measured on a live server.** The fix is pinned against the page's own write calls in the existing harness. The card's repro (showcase plus a writable QA package) was not re-run in a browser.
- **Rework (L1 comment 7224511994).** The restore now runs only for a failure known to have written nothing (M1). The second toast lists every restore reason (N1).

## Verification

Read first: the `handleSetDefault` catch block in `ui/apps/console/src/pages/system/AppManagementPage.tsx` (the restore loop), then the new describe in `AppManagementPage.mutations.test.tsx`.

Two-minute check: `pnpm --dir ui exec vitest run apps/console/src/pages/system/__tests__/AppManagementPage.mutations.test.tsx`. Expected result: all pass, including the cases under "a refused promote restores the previous default".
